response.consequence: If a calendar or video deletion fails (expired credentials, API error), the error becomes an unhandled rejection. That can crash the Node process or log nothing useful, and the intended try/catch logging is dead. Handlers can return before the old events are removed, leaving stale busy slots.
response.explanation: The change made the forEach callback async because getCalendar now returns a Promise. Array.forEach does not await the callback's promise. In vital/lib/reschedule.ts (125-128) and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts (125-128), the surrounding try/catch no longer catches errors from getCalendar, deleteEvent or deleteMeeting. Those errors become unhandled promise rejections. The same pattern is in bookings.tsx (the bookingRefsFiltered.forEach near line 553), where there is no catch at all. Previously the getCalendar call was synchronous. The deletions are also not awaited, so the reschedule flow continues (sending emails, webhooks, returning) before the calendar events are deleted.
